original_question: Does every effectively compact left-c.e. Polish space admit a computable, equivalently right-c.e., Polish copy?
target_in_paper: Section 8 (Keng Meng Selwyn Ng), Problem 26: "Does every (effectively) compact left-c.e. Polish space have a computable (right c.e.) Polish copy?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact open problem targeted in the paper: it concerns left-c.e. Polish spaces, focuses on the effectively compact case singled out in Problem 26, and asks whether such a space must admit a better homeomorphic presentation.
missing_details: The official formulation in the paper is parenthetical on both ends: it asks about "(effectively) compact" left-c.e. Polish spaces and about a "computable (right c.e.)" Polish copy.

The nearby context defines right-c.e. metric spaces, and says the left-c.e. notion is analogous: one should specify that the space is presented by a countable dense metric structure whose pairwise distances are uniformly left-c.e.
The phrase "Polish copy" should be made explicit as a homeomorphic Polish presentation of the same space, not a literally identical metric presentation.

Your phrase "equivalently right-c.e." is stronger than what the paper says. Problem 26 does not assert or prove that having a computable copy is equivalent to having a right-c.e. copy; it lists the right-c.e. version parenthetically as a weaker companion variant.
To make the question stand-alone, one should say what a "computable Polish copy" means: a Polish presentation with uniformly computable distances on a countable dense set.
Likewise, one should say what a "right-c.e. Polish copy" means: a Polish presentation with uniformly right-c.e. distances on a countable dense set.
The question is about existence of some better presentation up to homeomorphism; it does not ask for the homeomorphism itself to be computable.
The note itself does not unpack the effective-compactness hypothesis, so a fully stand-alone version should indicate that effective compactness is part of the given left-c.e. presentation.
refined_question: Let X be a Polish space that admits an effectively compact left-c.e. presentation, i.e. a presentation by a countable dense metric space whose distances are uniformly left-c.e. Must the homeomorphism type of X admit a computable Polish presentation? If not, must it at least admit a right-c.e. Polish presentation?
justification: Because arXiv:2507.03972 is an open-problems note, the nearest official target is Problem 26 itself. Your draft matches that problem very closely: the same hypothesis appears in the same section, and the same conclusion is asked for. The sentence immediately before Problem 26 gives the relevant left-/right-c.e. metric-space setup, and the sentence immediately after records the motivating comparison results. The one substantive correction is that the paper does not treat "computable" and "right-c.e." as equivalent here; it asks for a computable copy, with the right-c.e. version in parentheses as a weaker variant.
